newsitem.title: SRI LANKA: Sri Lanka government suffers blow on broadcast law.
newsitem.headline: Sri Lanka government suffers blow on broadcast law.

text.p: Sri Lanka's Supreme Court dealt a blow to the government by ruling that a bill to set up a powerful broadcasting authority was inconsistent with the constitution, parliament speaker K.B. Ratnayake said on Tuesday.
The bill, introduced in parliament last month, seeks to set up a broadcasting authority with wide powers to monitor, regulate and grant operating licences to radio and television broadcasters.

It was seen by opponents as an effort to stifle freedom of speech and was challenged in the Supreme Court by media watchdog the Free Media Movement (FMM), several private broadcasters and the opposition United National Party.

"The Supreme Court is of the view that some of the provisions of the bill are inconsistent with the provisions of the constitution and the bill as a whole is inconsistent with Article 10 of the constitution...," speaker Ratnayake said.
He said the ruling meant that in order for the bill to become law, it would need to be passed by a two-thirds majority in parliament, where the government has only a one-seat majority.
The Court's ruling also meant the bill would have to be put to a national referendum, he said.
The FMM has said the proposed authority would pave the way for complete control by the government over the emerging and expanding electronic media.

The bill says the annual renewal of broadcasting licences would need backing from the authority's board of directors, who will include senior officials from government departments, including the defence ministry.
